assumptions.note: Criteo publishes no campaign economics, so cost per impression and value per incremental conversion are explicit assumptions. The dashboard recomputes the whole allocation client-side, so any reader can substitute their own numbers.

rules: Do not target everyone. Past the point where the marginal user's incremental value falls below the impression cost, extra spend destroys profit even though it still adds conversions.
Rank by estimated treatment effect, not by predicted conversion. The response model spends on users who would have converted anyway.
Set the cutoff at tau(x) > cost / value. That single threshold is the profit-maximizing rule and needs no tuning.
Treat the optimum as a plateau, not a point. The profit curve is flat near its peak, so any budget inside the plateau is defensible and the exact argmax is not identified by this sample.
Budget against the interval, not the point estimate. The lower bound of the bootstrap band is the number to commit spend against.
